_note:
The scale ceiling. Everything measured before this was sized to be achievable, because the first question was whether a local model could do useful work at all. This asks the opposite: where does a mechanical change stop working?

One repository, one task shape, one variable. S1 is the size already known to pass. S3 against S4 is the point of the whole thing: near-identical reference counts, very different file spread, so a failure at S4 that S3 survives means the limit is file-hopping rather than volume. Those are different limits and different advice.

Verified by the target's own typecheck plus the old symbol being gone, which is unambiguous: either every reference moved or it did not.

tasks.prompt: Rename hentFrontendFeilmelding to hentBrukerFeilmelding everywhere in this repository, including its definition, every import, every call site and every test. Change nothing else.
tasks._why: The known-good size. Rung 3 passed this 8 of 8, so a failure here invalidates the run.

tasks.prompt: Rename useSidebarStore to useSidepanelStore everywhere in this repository, including its definition, every import, every call site and every test. Change nothing else.
tasks._why: Half again as many references at the same spread.

tasks.prompt: Rename behandlingILesemodus to behandlingErSkrivebeskyttet everywhere in this repository, including its definition, every import, every call site and every test. Change nothing else.
tasks._why: Six times the references and four times the spread of S1.

tasks.prompt: Rename useBehandlingState to useBehandlingTilstand everywhere in this repository, including its definition, every import, every call site and every test. Change nothing else.
tasks._why: Same volume as S3, nearly twice the spread. The comparison that separates volume from file-hopping.
